title: EIT HEI Call 2026: up to €1.25M for university-led deep-tech consortia
dek: The EIT Higher Education Initiative is funding HEI-led consortia that build deep-tech and manufacturing innovation capacity. Deadline: 13 January 2027.
key_facts: EIT Higher Education Initiative (EIT HEI), Call for Proposals 2026
5 partners, incl. 3 HEIs from 3 countries and 2 business partners
body: The EIT Higher Education Initiative opened its Call for Proposals 2026 on 20 October 2026. It funds projects that help universities and other higher education institutions turn STEM talent, knowledge and research into deep-tech and manufacturing innovation and entrepreneurship. Each project can receive up to €1.25 million over 18 months, from 1 May 2027 to 31 October 2028.

Projects are expected to work on three connected fronts: developing talent, strengthening the institution's capacity to valorise knowledge and innovate, and linking the institution to regional and European innovation ecosystems. Eligible activities include innovation action plans, entrepreneurship programmes, training and mentoring, new or stronger innovation structures inside the institution, technology transfer and start-up creation.

Applications come from consortia led by a higher education institution. The minimum is five organisations, all in Horizon Europe eligible countries, with at least three higher education institutions from three different countries (one of them in an EU Member State) and at least two business or industry partners, which may be networks or associations. Research organisations, transfer offices, public bodies, intermediaries, social enterprises and NGOs can also join.

Applicants complete the HEInnovate self-assessment and an Innovation Vision Action Plan, register in the EU Participant Portal and submit through the EIT HEI application portal. The deadline is 13 January 2027 at 17:00 CET, and results are due in March 2027. Online info sessions run until 3 December, covering KPI expectations, application and budget planning, an EIT KIC Discovery Day and an open Q&A.
why: Ullswater Investments analysis: the business-partner requirement is the detail to watch. Every consortium needs at least two companies or industry associations, so universities will be looking for industrial partners in deep tech and manufacturing over the next weeks, and companies have a direct route into university-led innovation projects. With a January deadline and two months left, the consortium should be closed in November so that December can go into the action plan and budget. Spanish universities that want to coordinate should start with the HEInnovate self-assessment, which shapes the rest of the proposal.
